title: Blockchain and cryptocurrencies
subtitle: Since 2009
subject: comprendreLeMonde
description: The **blockchain** invented a ledger that no one can tamper with alone, paving the way for a new digital economy.

hero.hook: A book of accounts that no one owns, but that thousands of computers monitor together.

blocks.text: Imagine a book of accounts that no one person owns, but that thousands of computers update at the same time, all over the world, and that it is almost impossible to falsify. This is the initial idea of ​​the **blockchain**, a technology often reduced to its first application, the **Bitcoin**.

By making it possible to exchange value without going through a bank, this invention gave rise to an entire parallel economy, between promises of financial freedom and severe criticism of its energy cost.

sections.title: A register that no one controls alone

blocks.text: At the heart of blockchain is a simple idea: the **distributed ledger**. Unlike a bank, which keeps its accounts on its own servers, the blockchain relies on a network of , that is to say thousands of computers which each keep an identical copy of all transactions. [[peers]]

The very first block of the Bitcoin blockchain, called the “genesis block”, contained a hidden message: the front page of a British newspaper on January 3, 2009, which spoke of the state bailout of the banks. A political nod from its creator.

Each transaction is first verified by the network and then grouped with others into a **block**. This block is then linked to the previous one thanks to a mathematical calculation called : a kind of unique digital fingerprint. The result is an uninterrupted chain of blocks, hence the name blockchain. To modify a single old transaction, you would have to recalculate the entire chain and convince more than half of the network, which is almost impossible on a large scale. [[hashing]]

sections.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum: from payment to program

blocks.text: The **Bitcoin**, launched in **2009** by an anonymous person (or group) under the name , proved that a monetary system could function without a central bank. To guarantee its scarcity, its creator has set a strict ceiling: never more than **21 million bitcoins** can exist, a bit like gold is limited on Earth. [[Satoshi Nakamoto]]

blocks.caption: Each transaction is verified by a network of computers before being added to the chain.

blocks.text: In 2015, a second generation of blockchain appeared with **Ethereum**. Its great innovation: **smart contracts**. These are programs that run automatically as soon as a condition is met, for example automatic reimbursement in the event of a train delay, without the need to go through an intermediary.

The success of cryptocurrencies is not without its problems. The most discussed concerns the **energy consumption** of the Bitcoin network: its annual electricity expenditure is today comparable to that of an entire country like Argentina.
The market also suffers from extreme **volatility**: the price of Bitcoin can vary by 10 or 20% in a few hours. This instability currently prevents it from becoming a real everyday currency.

Finally, the relative anonymity of transactions has sometimes been used for illegal activities. But the blockchain actually remains completely transparent: the authorities can follow the flow of money, which makes laundering more difficult than in the classic cash system.

Today, cryptocurrencies are leaving the margins to enter traditional finance. Large banks now offer to hold digital assets for their customers, and several states are considering creating their own official digital currency, a  (central bank digital currency). **[[MNBC]]**

**stablecoins**, cryptocurrencies whose price is stabilized thanks to a reserve of dollars or euros, serve as a bridge between the two worlds. Beyond finance, sectors such as luxury (to fight counterfeiting), logistics (to track containers) or health (to secure medical records) are also adopting blockchain for its reliability.
In 2021, El Salvador became the first country in the world to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender, alongside the US dollar, requiring every merchant to accept it if they have the technical means.

Created in 2009, the blockchain is a shared ledger that is almost impossible to falsify, with a maximum supply of bitcoins set at 21 million units. It laid the foundations of a new digital economy today in full institutional integration.
